title: Protocol measuring horizontal gene transfer from algae to non-photosynthetic organisms
author: Lee
materials: integrative genetic transformation through homologous recombination into the host genomic DNA. In a plasmid transformant, the transgenes such as an antibiotic-resistant transgene are in a self-replicable plasmid like pUC57 that can somehow replicate also in certain host cyanobacterial cell. The copy number of the plasmid per cell may vary depending on how well the plasmid could replicate in the cyanobacterial cell. During cyanobacterial cell division, the distribution of plasmid to the daughter cells may be random in nature. Consequently, plasmid transformants tend to be less stable than the genomic transformants whose transgenes are integrated into their genomic DNA. It is likely that the transgenes carried by a plasmid may be more mobile for HTG than those integrated into the cyanobacterial genomic DNA. The protocol may be used to test this feature by measuring HGT frequency for both the plasmid transgenes and/or genomic transgenes from GE cyanobacteria to E. coli. Examples of materials and strains preparation including plasmid preparation and genetic transformation of cyanobacteria such as Thermosynechococcus elongatus BP1 (BA000039.

for creation of GE cyanobacteria including GE T. elongatus BP1 (pKB plasmid transformant) has been experimentally demonstrated in the Lee Laboratory at Old Dominion University and recently reported in Ref. [1].

steps.title: Prepare donor plasmid with selectable marker
steps.instruction: Construct a special plasmid that carries the designer transgene(s) of interest together with an antibiotic selectable marker to be used as the donor in the horizontal gene transfer assay.

steps.title: Transform cyanobacteria via electroporation
steps.instruction: Introduce the plasmid (or genomic construct) into Thermosynechococcus elongatus BP1 (or other cyanobacteria) by electroporation, then select transformant colonies and verify insertion by PCR.

steps.title: Grow engineered cyanobacteria in BG‑11
steps.instruction: Photoautotrophically cultivate the genetically engineered T. elongatus BP1 in BG‑11 liquid medium until the culture reaches mid‑logarithmic growth phase.

steps.title: Grow wild‑type E. coli in LB
steps.instruction: Grow wild‑type Escherichia coli DH5α in liquid LB medium until the culture reaches mid‑logarithmic growth phase.

steps.title: Harvest cyanobacterial cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Collect the mid‑log phase GE T. elongatus BP1 cells by centrifugation using a Beckman Coulter Avanti J‑26 Xp centrifuge.

steps.title: Harvest E. coli cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Collect the mid‑log phase wild‑type E. coli cells by centrifugation using a Beckman Coulter Avanti J‑26 Xp centrifuge.

steps.title: Resuspend cyanobacteria to 10⁷ cells/mL
steps.instruction: Resuspend the harvested GE T. elongatus BP1 pellet in BG‑110SA liquid medium to obtain a cell density of approximately 1 × 10⁷ cells per milliliter.

steps.title: Resuspend E. coli to 10⁷ cells/mL
steps.instruction: Resuspend the harvested wild‑type E. coli DH5α pellet in LB liquid medium to obtain a cell density of approximately 1 × 10⁷ cells per milliliter.

steps.title: Mix donor and recipient suspensions 1:1
steps.instruction: Combine 15 mL of the cyanobacterial suspension (in BG‑110SA) with 15 mL of the E. coli suspension (in LB) to achieve a 1:1 population ratio.

steps.title: Co‑incubate mixture under light at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Place the 30 mL donor‑recipient mixture on a shaker set to 37 °C and expose it to continuous photosynthetic light intensity from daylight fluorescent lamps for the designated incubation time (tIncubation).

steps.title: Plate co‑culture samples with and without antibiotic
steps.instruction: From the incubation co‑culture, take aliquots and:

substeps.instruction: a) Plate samples on LB agar without antibiotic (control).
b) Plate samples on LB agar containing the appropriate antibiotic.
c) For each antibiotic plate, spread a designated volume (VIncubation), typically 100 µL, onto the surface of a 45 mL antibiotic‑containing LB agar plate.

steps.title: Incubate plates at 37 °C for colony development
steps.instruction: Incubate the plated LB agar dishes at 37 °C and monitor colony formation at 1, 2, 4, 7, and up to 14 days, including appropriate control plates.

steps.title: Count antibiotic‑resistant E. coli colonies
steps.instruction: Count the number of E. coli DH5α colonies (Ncolony) that appear on the antibiotic‑containing LB agar plates.

steps.title: Verify colonies by microscopy
steps.instruction: Examine the antibiotic‑resistant colonies using an Olympus DP672 microscope to confirm their morphology and presence of the transferred transgene (in combination with control experiments).

steps.title: Verify colonies by colony PCR
steps.instruction: Perform colony PCR on the antibiotic‑resistant colonies to confirm the presence of the donor transgene (in combination with control experiments).

steps.title: Calculate HGT frequency using provided equation
steps.instruction: Compute the horizontal gene transfer frequency with the formula: HGT Frequency = Ncolony / (VIncubation × CRecipient × tIncubation), where Ncolony is the colony count, VIncubation is the plated volume, CRecipient is the recipient cell concentration (≈1 × 10⁷ cells/mL), and tIncubation is the co‑incubation time.
